You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC learned rule

## Two-color frequency relabeling (verified: task-3cb64e1f)
For a grid with exactly two colors, map the more frequent color to the less frequent color, and map the less frequent color to 0, preserving positions and dimensions. Verified demos: 5-heavy with rare 6 → 5→6 and 6→0; 5-heavy with rare 4 → 5→4 and 4→0. Test confirmed 5→7 and 7→0. Do not assume fixed color identities; count each grid's frequencies. Detailed evidence in `memory/continual-arc-task-3cb64e1f.md`.

## Task pattern: uniform straight separators recolored
A demonstrated ARC transformation: identify complete uniform horizontal/vertical lines (including multi-cell-thick bands) that act as separators, and recolor those separator cells to 2 while leaving all other cells unchanged. In the observed demo, the input had a top row entirely color 4 and two adjacent full-height columns entirely color 4; output changed those row/column separator cells to 2. In its test, the separators were a full-height column of 0 and full-width rows of 0, and replacing precisely those cells with 2 solved the puzzle. Treat the geometry of complete straight separator bands as the invariant; the line color can vary.

## Task pattern: fill enclosed rectangle
For task-2c92d428, a single closed rectangular outline with dangling line extensions was filled in its interior with color 4; preserve the boundary, outside extensions, and rest of grid. Demo confirmed the fill color; test was accepted. Details and coordinates in `memory/continual-arc-task-2c92d428.md`. Infer fill color from demonstrations for other tasks.

# Continual-ARC task-2c92d428: fill enclosed rectangle

Verified on 2026-10-21 by a correct test submission.

## Rule
In a grid with a background, a line color, and an enclosed rectangular outline, fill the rectangle's interior with color 4. Keep the outline, all line extensions outside the rectangle, and all other cells unchanged. Identify the closed boundary from its four straight sides; do not fill the dangling extensions that may continue outward from the boundary.

## Evidence
Demo: 14x21 grid, background 2, outline color 0. The rectangle's boundary is rows 5 and 10, columns 16 and 20 (zero-based); fill only its interior rows 6–9, columns 17–19 with 4. Existing external extensions of the outline (vertical line above and horizontal line to the left) remain unchanged. Demo output confirms the fill color is 4.

Test: 19x10, background 7, outline color 1. Rectangle boundary rows 14 and 18, columns 2 and 6 (zero-based); interior rows 15–17, columns 3–5 filled with 4. The rest of the grid remained unchanged. Submission was accepted.

Likely reusable rule for tasks with a single enclosed rectangle; infer the fill color from demo rather than assuming 4 in unrelated tasks.
